about: Hand-made inputs for build_pairings.py: which caption rows are the quote, which donor statement it sits beside, who spoke and how that is supported, and every judgement made. Nothing here is a quote or a priority in itself: build_pairings.py re-reads the words from data/transcripts and data/priorities.json and refuses to build if they are not found there verbatim. Outside pages were read on the date given in read_on.

speaker.text_support: The row at 01:07:44 opens the turn with the member's name, legibly spelled: 'SUPERVISOR MELGAR THANK YOU MR. PRESIDENT.' The remarks then say 'SEND THIS MEASURE TO THE BALLOT TODAY' directly after the clerk's reading of the Housing Trust Fund charter amendment (rows 01:07:20 to 01:07:38).
speaker.doubt_reason: Name spelled correctly in the cue, district 7 is not stated in the text but the surname is unique on the roster.

outside.says: SPUR's voter guide says Supervisor Melgar and Mayor Lurie introduced Prop C, the Housing Trust Fund charter amendment.
The San Francisco Examiner reports Melgar wants to send a charter amendment to voters raising the Housing Trust Fund target from about $50 million to $125 million.

pairings.overlap: Same measure: Prop C, the Housing Trust Fund charter amendment, and the same figure ($125 million).
pairings.stance: Same side on the text: the quote asks colleagues to send the measure to the ballot and the donor's statement says it supports Prop C. (My reading of the quote; the donor's side is its own words.)

judgement.note: Shared named thing ('Housing Trust Fund', '$125 million', 'Prop C') surfaces the pair.
Rows 01:07:48 to 01:08:14 chosen as the first sentences of the member's remarks.
The spoken-cue rule proposes Melgar; a person confirmed the cue opens the turn.
Read the donor statement to confirm it states a position ('supports Prop C').
data/committees.json; own candidate and officeholder committees only.
Names returned by the money query must be read to confirm they are the Chamber and not a namesake.

check_next: Whether the Chamber's Prop C statement and Melgar's remarks are two independent routes to the same measure, or the same coalition (the measure's co-sponsors and endorsers).
The dates of any Chamber contribution against the dates of the meeting and of the Chamber's page (2026-10-08), read as dates and nothing more.
pairings.subject: Prop C, the Housing Trust Fund

speaker.text_support: The row at 00:15:38 opens the turn: 'SUPERVISOR CHEN THANK YOU FOR PRESENT.' The member then says 'MY CHARTER AMENDMENT TO ESTABLISH A MUNICIPAL FINANCIAL CORPORATION AND PUBLIC BANK'. The caption surname CHEN is one letter from CHAN (District 1) and the transcript text alone does not separate them; the member's own claim to the public bank charter amendment is what points to Chen.
speaker.doubt_reason: One-letter surname pair on the Board (Chan D1, Chen D11). Resolved only by outside sources naming Chen as the charter amendment's sponsor.

outside.says: The San Francisco Chronicle reports Supervisor Chyanne Chen will introduce a charter amendment establishing a municipal financial corporation (the public bank plan).
KALW reports that Supervisor Chyanne Chen promoted Prop B at a June Board of Supervisors meeting (read as a search extract).
GrowSF's own Prop B page lists the sponsor as Supervisor Chen, co-sponsored by Supervisors Fielder, Melgar, Mahmood and Walton.

pairings.overlap: Same measure: Prop B, the Municipal Finance Corporation and public bank, named in the quote as 'municipal financial corporation and public bank' (the caption's wording).
pairings.stance: Different positions on the text: the official describes her own charter amendment; the donor recommends voting No on B. (My reading.)

judgement.note: Shared named thing ('public bank', 'Municipal Finance Corporation', Prop B).
Rows 00:15:56 to 00:16:27, cut at the end of the sentence. The same speech also speaks to Prop C; only the sentence about the public bank is the pair.
The cue rule proposes a name, but Chen against Chan cannot be settled from the caption text; outside sponsor records settle it.
The quote describes the measure and the speaker's authorship; it does not itself say how the speaker will vote. Recorded as stated.
data/committees.json lists one committee for Chen: Chyanne Chen for Supervisor 2024 (terminated).
Names returned by the money query must be read.

check_next: Whether the official's committee filed after 2024; the committee list is a snapshot (terminated committee), so money to a newer committee would not be found.
Whether any contribution from the donor to the sponsor's committee was reported at all, and in which filing.
pairings.subject: Prop B, the public bank

speaker.text_support: The chair is told at 02:52:22 'TODAY WE HAVE SUPERVISOR' and the next row reads 'BALA MAMU HERE.' The caption renders the name phonetically, which no spelling match to the roster reaches. The member thanks 'MY CO SPONSORS SUPERVISOR DORSEY MELGAR, CHEN WANG AND WALTON' at 02:53:17 to 02:53:24, naming others and not himself, and the item read at 02:51:39 is the foreclosure-exemption transfer tax measure.
speaker.doubt_reason: The speaker's name is captioned phonetically ('BALA MAMU'), so no cue spells a roster surname. The cue rule's own proposal rests on another cue, the committee chair ('CHAIR CHIN'), and names the wrong person. Credit rests on the item reading, the co-sponsor list and the sponsor record outside the transcript, and the donor's own page naming Supervisor Mahmood as the measure's sponsor.

outside.says: The Department of Elections' legal text for the measure lists the sponsors as Supervisor Mahmood; Dorsey, Melgar, Chen, Wong, Walton, Mandelman (file 260692).
The San Francisco Examiner reports Supervisor Bilal Mahmood introduced the November ballot measure eliminating the transfer tax exemption on larger foreclosures.

pairings.overlap: Same measure and same subject: the foreclosure exemption in the real property transfer tax (Prop J) and how the market has changed since the exemption was written.
pairings.stance: Same side on the text: the quote presents the measure as bringing the transfer tax code up to date, and the donor's statement is on its page for Prop J, labelled 'Yes'. (My reading of the quote; the label is on the donor's page.)

judgement.note: Shared named thing ('transfer tax', 'foreclosure exemption').
Rows 02:52:31 to 02:52:42, the first two sentences after the greeting.
The rule proposes the committee chair from another cue (wrong) and nobody for the garbled name. A person used the item reading, the co-sponsor list and the outside sponsor record.
Checked the donor page for Prop J: GrowSF's page is labelled 'Yes'. A different donor statement on the same page (P108) argues against objections to the measure.
data/committees.json: Bilal Mahmood for Supervisor 2024 (active) and for DCCC Member 2024.
Names returned by the money query must be read.

check_next: The sponsor's measure was introduced after the 2024 election; look for the donor in the sponsor's 2026 filings (filed after the snapshot of committees) as well as the committees listed.
Whether the donor's own endorsement page and the sponsor's remarks quote the same Assessor-Recorder figures, which would point to a shared source rather than to each other.
pairings.subject: Prop J, the foreclosure transfer tax exemption

speaker.text_support: Same turn as pairing 3, 40 seconds on. The caption has a '>>' mark at 02:53:29, which the transcript survey found is not a reliable speaker change (it also appears inside one member's remarks). The text continues the sponsor's thanks ('FOR THEIR SUPPORT AS WELL') into 'THIS MEASURE COMES AT A CRITICAL MOMENT'.
speaker.doubt_reason: Same garbled cue as pairing 3, plus a '>>' mark immediately before the passage that could be a change of speaker. The cue rule proposes Dorsey, from the thanks to co-sponsors in the rows just before the passage, which is wrong.

outside.says: The Department of Elections' legal text for the measure lists the sponsors as Supervisor Mahmood; Dorsey, Melgar, Chen, Wong, Walton, Mandelman (file 260692).

pairings.overlap: Same measure: Prop J. Both speak to what the measure does to the city's revenue given the budget deficit.
pairings.stance: Different positions on the text: the quote presents closing the exemption as 'not about creating a new tax', while the donor recommends voting No on J and says the measure raises taxes. (My reading.)

judgement.note: Shared named thing and shared phrases (budget, revenue, tax).
Rows from 02:53:29 (cut at the phrase) to 02:53:57.
The rule proposes Dorsey (wrong, from the thanks to co-sponsors). A person had to decide the '>>' mark is not a change of speaker, which the text cannot show.
The Blueprint statement states a position ('We recommend voting No on J').
As pairing 3.
Names returned by the money query must be read.

check_next: Whether the sponsor and the donor had a common source for the revenue figures (the Controller's estimate) rather than a connection to each other.
pairings.subject: Prop J, the foreclosure transfer tax exemption

speaker.text_support: Walton is called at 02:36:50 ('SUPERVISOR WALTON THANK YOU, MADAM CLERK'), says 'I AM INTRODUCING A RESOLUTION AND ALSO A BILL A REQUEST', and the request here is the 'also'. The remarks say 'DISTRICT TEN RESIDENTS' and 'DISTRICT TEN WILL SOON FACE' (District 10 is Walton on the roster) and thank 'SUPERVISOR CHEN AS WELL AS SUPERVISOR FIELDER', so the speaker is neither of those. The chair moves on at 02:42:48 ('THE REST I SUBMIT ... SUPERVISOR WALTON. SUPERVISOR HUANG SUBMIT').
speaker.doubt_reason: No name cue directly before the passage (the cue is 3 minutes earlier, with '>>' marks between). The cue rule proposes Fielder, from the thanks to Supervisors Chen and Fielder in the rows just before, which is wrong. The speaker's own 'District Ten' and the chair's closing agree with Walton.

pairings.overlap: Same measure: Prop E, the City Administrator's authority over procurement and term, named in the quote as 'extending the City Administrator's term to ten years while giving that office authority over procurement'.
pairings.stance: Different positions on the text: the quote asks the Budget and Legislative Analyst for a cost analysis of the measures and says they 'shift real power away from the Board of Supervisors'; the donor's statement says it supports Prop E. (My reading.)

judgement.note: Shared named thing ('City Administrator', 'procurement', '10 years').
Rows 02:39:58 (cut at the phrase) to 02:40:56.
The rule proposes Fielder (wrong: she is thanked in the rows before the passage). A person read 3 minutes of captions either side, including the speaker's reference to 'District Ten'.
Read the donor statement for Prop E and the Prop F statement (P039); a second pairing from the same speech is possible with P039.
data/committees.json lists six committees for Walton, all terminated; one is a committee formed to support him (not his own).
Names returned by the money query must be read.

check_next: Whether Walton's committees since 2022 are missing from the snapshot of committees; his current-cycle committee may not be in the list.
Whether the donor's committees gave to the measure's committees that Walton's remarks are about, which is a different filing question from gifts to Walton.
pairings.subject: Prop E, City Administrator powers

speaker.text_support: At 02:56:31 to 02:56:34 a member asks who made the motion to rescind the vote: 'A SUPERVISOR CHEN MAKE THE MOTION TO RESCIND A VOTE'. At 02:57:14 a member says 'WHY SHE WOULD HAVE LIKED THE ITEM TO BE RESCINDED' and at 02:57:22 'IF SHE CHOOSES A SUPERVISOR CHANCE TO ANSWER'. The passage answers that question, in the first person.
speaker.doubt_reason: The call-out spells the surname 'CHANCE' and the earlier mention 'CHEN'. The cue rule reads 'CHANCE' as Chan (District 1), which is wrong; Chen against Chan is a one-letter pair. Credit rests on the preceding question naming the member who moved the rescission. No minutes were read to confirm who moved it.

pairings.overlap: Same subject: the cut in the inclusionary housing fee that the Board passed on 14 July 2026, set against the Housing Trust Fund. The donor's statement describes the cut ('the Board delivered the first half on July 14, 2026, when it cut the tax from 15% to 5%').
pairings.stance: Different positions on the text: the quote says the speaker is not supporting the legislation; the donor's statement describes the same legislation as the first half of a deal on its Prop C page, labelled 'Yes'. (My reading.)

judgement.note: Shared phrases ('Housing Trust Fund', 'inclusionary').
The rule proposes Chan from the garbled 'CHANCE' (wrong). Credit comes from the question that precedes the answer.
The quote states a position on the legislation (item 39). That the donor's sentence is about the same legislation is my reading of its description of 'the tax' cut to 5%.
As pairing 2.
Names returned by the money query must be read.

check_next: The minutes of 14 July 2026 for who moved to rescind item 39 and the vote on it, which would settle the speaker credit.
The text of item 39 against the donor's description of the 15% to 5% cut.
pairings.subject: inclusionary housing fees and the Housing Trust Fund

dropped.why: Great Highway ballot remark. The caption rows 01:48:49 to 01:49:16 show a member of the public ('MY NAME IS MOLLY ... OUTER MAMAS') giving public comment; this is not an official's statement.

The donor statement P043 says the Chamber 'has abstained from taking a position on Prop J'; there is no position to pair. The passage also reads (my reading) as a report of the Assessor-Recorder's data and no speaker cue was found for it.

'IN THEIR OPINION, THE MEASURE WOULD SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASE ...' relays an analyst's estimate ('THEIR OPINION'); not the official's own statement of view. The earlier trial's labelled 'meaningful' rested on topic alone.
A supporting speech for Prop C with no name cue within the 40 words before it and none in the rows after; speaker not found from the transcript text.
A speech on the technical advisory committee's report with no cue; speaker not found.

The same speech as pairing 2, continued: it says 'I'M GOING TO SUPPORT THIS THIS AFTERNOON BUT ... I CANNOT SAY THAT I WON'T ADVOCATE AGAINST THIS'. Usable as a further pairing with P036 once the speaker credit in pairing 2 stands; not used, to keep one pairing per speech passage.
The same speech as pairing 5, Prop F (executive branch management); a spare pairing against the Chamber's Prop F statement.
